factual: There are 60 minutes in an hour and 60 seconds in a minute.
There are 24 hours in a day, 7 days in a week and 52 weeks in a year.
A year has 12 months and 365 days (366 in a leap year).
A dozen is 12 items; half a dozen is 6.
There are 100 cents in a dollar; a quarter is 25 cents, a dime 10 cents, a nickel 5 cents.
There are 12 inches in a foot, 3 feet in a yard and 5280 feet in a mile.
There are 16 ounces in a pound and 1000 grams in a kilogram.
There are 4 quarts in a gallon and 1000 milliliters in a liter.
A week has 5 weekdays and 2 weekend days.
procedural: Percent of a quantity: part = whole * percent / 100.
Increase by p percent: new = old * (1 + p / 100). Decrease by p percent: new = old * (1 - p / 100).
Profit = revenue - cost; revenue = price per unit * units sold.
Average = sum of the values / number of values.
Rate problems: distance = speed * time; total work = rate * time.
'k times as many as x' means k * x; 'k more than x' means x + k; 'k fewer than x' means x - k.
Half of x is x / 2; a third of x is x / 3; a fraction a/b of x is x * a / b.
To split a total evenly into groups: per group = total / groups; leftover = total % groups.
Total cost of several items = sum of (quantity * unit price) for each item.
Work backwards: if after an operation the result is known, apply the inverse operations in reverse order.
causal: Buying more items at a fixed unit price increases the total cost proportionally.
If something is given away, eaten, sold or lost, the remaining amount decreases by that quantity.
Earning money or receiving items increases the amount a person has.
A discount reduces the price paid; tax or a tip increases the amount paid.
